correctness.rationale: After positive-affine normalization to weighted mean zero and variance one, any interior extremum of the third central moment on a stratum with at least three distinct support levels would satisfy a quadratic stationarity equation at every distinct level, which is impossible at three or more points unless the multiplier system degenerates; the mean and variance constraint gradients are independent on every nondegenerate stratum. Hence a global extremum descends to a two-level boundary. A cut after index \(j\) has lower mass \(P_j\) and skewness \(g(P_j)=(2P_j-1)/\sqrt{P_j(1-P_j)}\). Since \(g\) is strictly increasing, the closure extrema are attained at the first and last cuts, giving \(g(p_1)\) and \(g(1-p_m)\). Strict support makes both bounds unattained, while connectedness and continuity give the full open interval. The two-point case and \(\operatorname{Cov}(\bar X,S^2)=\mu_3/n\) corollary are standard exact identities and are consistent with the inspected verifier.
residual_risks: The theorem fixes the atom masses and varies only ordered support locations; it does not optimize jointly over masses.
The argument uses closure strata with coincident support values, so the strict-support conclusion is necessarily an open range rather than a closed one.
